notes: Letter-by-letter is a wave now: the word being sung is full gold, the word just sung holds its letters at half strength and the one before it at a whisper, so a run of light travels along the line and is gone two words behind it.

The wave no longer stops at a line: the word that was still lit when the sheet moved on keeps its letters for the same two-word trail, so the light travels from line to line instead of starting again at each one.

A sheet with no timings used to be spaced evenly, line count against the clock, so a short intro or a repeated chorus moved every line after it - slow through one part and fast through the next. The lines are laid out by their own words now.

A song with an instrumental in it stops drifting: the measured quiet stretches are cut out of the timeline the lines are spread over, so the words skip the break the way the voice does instead of drifting through it.

The player still says where each line starts, and now it also says where one may not: a snap can no longer park a line on a drum hit inside a measured instrumental, the same rule the AI timing already followed.
A timing you pinned by hand with Line up still outranks every measurement, and a song whose words are unchanged keeps the highlight it had. Nothing here touches the words themselves.
